content.text:
Section 6.1 is the only restriction binding the Company. Assessing it against the fallback:

- **Named/defined scope**: limited to "Deerskin Products" (a defined term excluding closeouts and Joan Cook Catalog) and named comparators (Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled) — not an undefined "any competing business."
- **Medium-limited**: only "any project similar to the Site on the Internet" — no restraint on catalog, wholesale or retail channels.
- **Term only**: "during the term of this Agreement" — no post-term tail, and the term is a 12-month period (§4.1) terminable on 90 days' notice.
- **Carve-outs**: §6.2 (closeout web site), the Deerskin Products definition, and §8(b) (Globix Agreement).
- **Direction**: the reciprocal restriction in §6.3 binds HDI *and* carries a two-year post-term tail — the asymmetry favors us.

This meets the fallback on every material term, so it should not be redlined.

input.quote: 6.1 Except as provided in Section 6.2, during the term of this Agreement, the Company shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products or products substantially similar to Deerskin Products (including, without limitation, the products of Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled and companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled) and HDI shall have the exclusive right to use of the "Deerskin" brand for a self-contained web site for the offering of Deerskin Products directly to the consumer on the Internet.
input.rationale: Section 6.1 does impose a field-of-use restriction on the Company (our client), so the preferred position (no restriction at all) is not met. However, it sits squarely at the playbook fallback and should not be redlined. (1) Scope is limited to a named product set: the defined term "Deerskin Products" (which expressly excludes closeout merchandise and the Joan Cook Catalog per §1.1) plus named comparators Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled — this is not an undefined "any competing business." (2) It is further confined to a single medium and format — "any project similar to the Site on the Internet" — leaving the Company's catalog, wholesale and bricks-and-mortar channels wholly unrestricted. (3) It runs "during the term of this Agreement" only, with no post-term tail, and the term under §4.1 is a one-year period auto-renewing annually and terminable by either Party on 90 days' notice, so the restraint is effectively capped at 12 months and we hold a unilateral exit. (4) Carve-outs exist: §6.2 preserves the Company's right to run its own closeout web site, the Deerskin Products definition excludes Joan Cook products, and §8(b) protects the existing Globix Agreement. Direction also favors us: the reciprocal covenant in §6.3 binds HDI on broader terms, with a two-year post-term tail that the Company does not bear, and the restriction is the consideration for HDI's exclusive-brand bargain. Nothing here approaches walk-away territory (no post-term non-compete and no undefined scope). Two minor sub-elements fall short of the preferred wording and are noted rather than flagged: there is no express carve-out for internal development or for businesses acquired by the Company, and "products substantially similar to Deerskin Products" is somewhat elastic. If this agreement is reopened for other reasons, we would add an acquisitions/internal-development carve-out to §6.2, but neither point is material enough to justify a redline on its own.
